# Industry Newsletter Digest — Week of May 11–16, 2026
Generated: 2026-05-16 | Sources: Travel Media Briefing (email, May 11), Travel Industry Insider #112 (email, May 13), Skyscanner Insights Blog (RSS, May 12), Creator Economy Law Watch (RSS, May 10), Travel PR Wire (RSS, May 7 & 9), Substack Blog (RSS, May 8), Affiliate Insider Travel (RSS, May 11), Mediavine Blog (RSS, May 6), Destination Marketing Weekly (RSS, May 13)

---

## 1. DESTINATION TRENDS

**Lisbon demand surge — directly relevant to current trip (May 12–19)**
- Lisbon is #1 or #2 most-searched European city for summer 2026 across Skyscanner and Kayak data, up 34% YoY. Shoulder-season and slow-travel content formats outperforming peak-summer itineraries in organic search. (Sources: Skyscanner Insights Blog RSS-901; Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)
- Azores emerging as secondary Portugal destination — search volume up 41% since Jan 2026. Potential content extension angle post-Lisbon trip. (Source: Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)
- Morocco/Marrakech press trip activity surging, partly driven by new Lisbon–Marrakech direct flights (TAP). 'Lisbon to Morocco' queries up 67% YoY — strong multi-destination angle for future content. (Source: Destination Marketing Weekly RSS-908)

**Southeast Asia & slow travel**
- Thailand and Vietnam leading Q3/Q4 2026 travel inquiry surge; Bangkok and Hoi An top Instagram Reels engagement. (Source: Travel Media Briefing MSG-5017)
- 'Slow travel' content outperforming fast-itinerary formats across Pinterest and YouTube — avg watch time up 22% for 7-day+ guides. Reinforces current editorial direction. (Source: Travel Media Briefing MSG-5017)

---

## 2. AFFILIATE & MONETIZATION NEWS

**FTC disclosure update — ACTION ITEM**
- FTC reaffirmed that newsletter affiliate links require 'clear and conspicuous' disclosure adjacent to each link in body copy. Footer-only disclosure is insufficient. Applies to all audience sizes; enforcement priority on 10K+ subscriber lists. Audit newsletter template before next send. (Source: Creator Economy Law Watch RSS-902; Travel Media Briefing MSG-5017)

**Booking.com Creator Dashboard (beta)**
- New real-time conversion tracking dashboard rolling out for affiliates with 10K+ monthly unique referrals. Features: per-campaign attribution, audience segmentation, A/B link testing, payout forecasting. General availability Q3 2026. Apply via Partner Hub. (Source: Affiliate Insider Travel RSS-906)

**Newsletter sponsorship CPMs**
- Travel newsletter CPMs averaging $42–$68 per 1,000 opens in Q2 2026 (Paved marketplace). Engaged lists under 20K still commanding premium rates. Relevant context for Q2 sponsorship package pricing. (Source: Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)

**Mediavine RPM up 15% Q1 2026**
- Travel content RPMs up 15% YoY; long-form 2,000+ word content up 22%. Passive revenue opportunity if site traffic grows. (Source: Mediavine Blog RSS-907)

**Impact.com affiliate compliance trend**
- Impact.com reports 27% increase in travel affiliate sign-ups YTD; brands prioritizing creators with verified disclosure compliance records. Reinforces value of current disclosure standards. (Source: Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)

---

## 3. PRESS TRIP & PARTNERSHIP OPPORTUNITIES

**Tourism New Zealand — South Island, August 2026**
- Open call for creators with 10K+ engaged following. 10-day itinerary: Queenstown, Fiordland, Catlins, Christchurch. Flights not covered. Deadline: June 30, 2026. Apply: tourismnewzealand.example/creator-press-trips (Source: Travel PR Wire RSS-903)

**Visit Scotland — Highland & Islands, July–August 2026**
- Solo/couple creators; editorial pitch + audience demographics required. US/Canada/Australia/Germany audiences prioritized. Deadline: May 28, 2026 — URGENT, only 12 days away. Apply: visitscotland.example/trade/press-trips (Source: Travel PR Wire RSS-905)

**Jordan Tourism Board — Petra + Wadi Rum, September 2026**
- Partnering with mid-tier travel media outlets. Expressions of interest through June 15. (Source: Travel Media Briefing MSG-5017)

**Airbnb Experiences creator program expansion**
- Now open to newsletter and blog-based creators (previously social-only). Info session webinar: May 22, 2026. (Source: Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)

**Morocco — ONMT 'Gateway to Africa' creator program**
- Running through Q3 2026; Marrakech Riad Association offering hosted stays for 15K+ creators. Strong Lisbon content extension angle. (Source: Destination Marketing Weekly RSS-908)

**SATW Annual Conference — Nashville, October 2026**
- Early-bird registration closes May 31, 2026. (Source: Travel Media Briefing MSG-5017)

---

## 4. MEDIA INDUSTRY UPDATES

**Substack travel growth**
- Travel newsletters top-5 fastest-growing Substack category in Q1 2026. Avg paid conversion rate 4.2% (vs. 3.1% platform-wide). Geographic-focus newsletters show highest retention. Potential discovery channel alongside primary Mailchimp list. (Source: Substack Blog RSS-904)

**Condé Nast Traveler restructuring**
- Digital editorial team restructuring; freelance contributor rates under review with possible upward revision for long-form. Monitor for pitch opportunities. (Source: Travel Media Briefing MSG-5017)

**ASJA freelance rate guide update**
- American Society of Journalists and Authors publishing updated freelance rate guide June 2026 — first revision since 2023. Useful for contract negotiations. (Source: Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)

**Google Travel Insights creator dashboard**
- Updated with creator-specific destination trend data by content format (video, article, newsletter). Free access. (Source: Travel Industry Insider MSG-5018)

---

## NOISE / EXCLUDED
- MSG-5019: TravelGear Weekly promotional email (40% off packing cubes + affiliate pitch) — commercial noise, excluded
- MSG-5020: Pack Your Bags PR cold pitch (Kenya safari press trip) — unsolicited cold outreach, excluded

---

## PRIORITY FOLLOW-UPS FROM THIS DIGEST
1. FTC disclosure audit — review newsletter template for per-link disclosure compliance before Thursday send (May 21)
2. Visit Scotland application — deadline May 28; draft pitch this week while Lisbon trip content is fresh
3. Booking.com Creator Dashboard — check referral volume eligibility for beta access
4. SATW early-bird registration — closes May 31

This is a coherent latent intent, not random noise. Nina has repeatedly circled back to the same workflow problem across four services (gmail, todo, scheduler, claw_notion) without completing any single action. The intent is real; the execution gap is consistent.

> "This trip was hosted by Visit Lisbon in partnership with Nina Caldwell Media. All opinions are my own."

- Blog posts: disclosure at TOP, before body text

title: Roam & Earn Early-Bird Decision — Working Notes (2026-02-24)
content:
Working notes from the Feb 24 budget review block (EVT-323).

## The Question
Should I commit to Roam & Earn Phase 1 at the early-bird rate ($240) before the Feb 27 deadline, or wait for the Wanderluxe installment to clear?

## Key Numbers
- Current confirmed Q2 sponsorship revenue: $1,050
- Current confirmed affiliate budget cap (20%): $210
- Wanderluxe Installment #1 pending: $450 (due March 5, clears March 3–5)
- Post-installment cap: $300
- Phase 1 early-bird: $240 (non-refundable, deadline Feb 27)
- Phase 1 standard: $300 (available from March 1)
- Price delta: $60

## The Problem
The installment clears AFTER the early-bird deadline. Committing now at $240 against a $210 cap = $30 over policy. Non-refundable.

## Risk Math
- Probability installment clears before Feb 27: ~15% (Wanderluxe confirmed March 1 batch processing)
- Expected overspend if I commit now: ~85% × $30 = ~$25.50
- Opportunity cost of waiting: $60 (certain)

On pure expected value, waiting costs more ($60 certain vs. ~$25.50 expected). BUT — the overspend isn't really probabilistic here. Wanderluxe literally told me they process on March 1. The installment will NOT clear before Feb 27. It's near-certain, not 85%.

## Decision
HOLD. The $60 opportunity cost is real and it stings, but committing $240 against a $210 cap when I know the installment won't clear in time is a policy violation, not a calculated risk. The policy exists for a reason — I've had months where expected income didn't materialize.

Plan: Reply to Sophie today, explain I'm holding pending a payment clearance, ask if she can informally hold a standard-rate slot until March 5. Worst case I pay $300 instead of $240. That's fine.

## Next Steps
- Reply to Sophie (MSG-5071) — today
- Watch for Wanderluxe clearance week of March 3
- Commit Phase 1 at $300 once confirmed
- Update NPAG-33 and WB-6
